To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the GTP- and InsP3-regulatory processes are both sensitive to the Ca2+-ATPase inhibitor thapsigargin.
InsP3-induced release of Ca2+ from the intracellular Ca2+ pool occurs through a GTP-regulatable mechanism.
GTP activates Ca2+ influx into a Ca2+ pool that is also released by InsP3.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the mechanisms that control Ca2+ entry and release from the intracellular Ca2+ pools.
the mechanisms of intracellular Ca2+ mobilization in mammalian cells.
the regulation of intracellular Ca2+ movements in mammalian cells and the role of these processes in cellular function.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
GTP regulates Ca2+ translocation into the InsP(3)-releasable pool and that this process is a key regulatory mechanism for the InsP(1,4, 5)P(3)-mediated Ca(2+) signaling pathway.
the GTP-regulated calcium translocating mechanism controls the calcium entry into the inositole trisphosphate-releasing calcium pool.
InsP3-induced release of Ca2+ from the InsP3-sensistive pool is regulated by a GTP-dependent Ca2+ influx mechanism, which may be important in the control of InsP3-induced intracellular Ca2+ signals.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the inositol trisphosphate-sensitive Ca2+ store is a subcompartment within the endoplasmically reticulum and that it is regulated by a GTP-dependent Ca2+-translocation mechanism.
GTP is a regulator for the InsP3 receptor, a Ca2+ channel, and a Ca2+ ATPase.
the inositol trisphosphate (IP3)-releasable Ca(2+)-pool is directly regulated by a GTP-dependent Ca(2+) translocating mechanism.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a GTP-dependent mechanism regulates the Ca2+ content of the InsP 3-releas able pool.
the InsP(3) receptor is not a passive Ca(2+)-release channel, but is an active, GTP-dependent, Ca(2+) pump.
a GTP-dependent Ca2+ translocating process is involved in the control of the InsP(3)-releasable Ca(2+)-pool.
